subject: Azure marketplace private offer — channel margin & SKU packaging alignment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma@datalyft.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Azure marketplace private offer — initial SKU & margin note

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Based on the usage profile you shared (steady ingest + 2x burst windows), I sketched a lightweight private-offer structure on Azure that keeps list-price intact while giving DataLyft a predictable blended effective discount.

Key points:
- Proposal: 12-month private offer (Azure Marketplace) using reserved-node SKU + metered token add-ons.
- Target effective discount to DataLyft: ~22% on committed node hours across the blend.
- Channel: you mentioned CloudBridge will resell; we typically accommodate a reseller uplift (channel margin) in the private-offer waterfall.

Attached: sku_mapping.xlsx (SKU -> our internal reserved capacity mapping + suggested commit bands).

Before I send a formal private-offer document to procurement, two asks so I build the PO correctly:
1) Confirm the reseller entity (CloudBridge?) and the margin you expect to keep (industry-standard is 10–20%).
2) Any required invoicing path (send to DataLyft vs. CloudBridge)?

If you want, we can jump on a quick 20-min call this afternoon to lock these details.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133

Attachment: sku_mapping.xlsx (excel, 48KB)

From: Emma Lin <emma@datalyft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace private offer — initial SKU & margin note

Karthik —

Thanks for the outline and the mapping file. Quick answers:
- Yes, CloudBridge will be our reseller for marketplace transactions. They handle the invoicing and take a standard reseller fee.
- Our procurement team needs clarity on the channel margin and how it shows up in the private-offer waterfall so we can justify to finance.

Two questions from procurement (cc'd procurement@datalyft.com):
1) Can Redwood structure the private offer so the reseller uplift is explicit (line-item) rather than baked into list price? It helps our cost-reconciliation.
2) What guideline should we provide CloudBridge on acceptable margin % — we were thinking 15% but need to know if that creates any downstream knock-on (e.g., Azure billing mapping or tax handling).

If you can send a redlineable PO that shows the margin carve-out, that would speed approval.

- Emma
Head of Platform Partnerships | DataLyft
emma@datalyft.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: (internal)
Date: 2027-05-25T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Azure marketplace private offer — initial SKU & margin note

Karthik / Laura —

Forwarding Emma's procurement questions. Quick ops note on channel-margin modeling so we give procurement something concrete:

Summary guidance (recommended):
- Reseller uplift: model a 15% reseller margin as a separate waterfall line in the private-offer metadata. This keeps the Azure list price intact and makes accounting straightforward for DataLyft.
- Invoice path: issue invoice to CloudBridge (reseller) with a short description mapping to DataLyft's billing reference. CloudBridge will then invoice DataLyft per their agreement.
- Tax/treatment: discouraging embedding the margin into list price avoids surprises on Azure tax handling and Marketplace reporting.

Example waterfall (for ops to include in PO):
- Gross list price (Azure SKU)
- Platform discount (Redwood private-offer effective discount)
- Reseller uplift (explicit 15% of gross list) — appears as reseller fee in metadata
- Net payable (Azure Marketplace settlement flows to Redwood/CloudBridge as configured)

I can prepare a redlineable PO template that includes the waterfall and a short note explaining why line-item uplifts are cleaner for reconciliation.

Attaching: none (small draft will live in Drive).

-Camila
Partner & Deal Ops | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma@datalyft.com>, DataLyft Procurement <procurement@datalyft.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace private offer — channel margin & SKU packaging alignment

Emma / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clarity. Per Camila's recommendation, Redwood is comfortable structuring the private offer with an explicit reseller uplift line. Proposed agreement points:

- Reseller uplift: 15% of gross list price (explicit line-item in the private-offer metadata).
- Invoice routing: Redwood will list CloudBridge as the reseller on the Marketplace transaction; Redwood will accept settlement to CloudBridge per the reseller arrangement and issue CloudBridge an invoice that maps to DataLyft PO ref.
- Tax: reseller will be responsible for reseller-side tax treatment; Redwood will provide the marketplace settlement reports for reconciliation.

Next steps I will take today:
1) Attach a redlineable PO (DataLyft_PO_v3.pdf) that includes the waterfall and a short billing note — please review and send back comments.
2) Share a DocuSign envelope when procurement confirms the PO header (linked here: https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC1234DLFT).
3) Camila / Ops will confirm the marketplace metadata fields we need from CloudBridge to ensure Azure routing is correct (SKU mapping / reseller tax id).

If procurement is comfortable with the 15% uplift, I'll prepare the private-offer in the Azure Marketplace and loop CloudBridge on next steps. Open to a 20-min sync if you prefer to walk through the PO line-by-line.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to make sure your finance team has clean artifacts for approval.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
